The merge applies the second task vector against the already-merged tensor instead of the unmodified base: `tmp = b + λ(f1−b)` then `out = tmp + λ(f2−tmp)`, which expands to `0.36·b + 0.24·f1 + 0.4·f2` rather than the required `0.2·b + 0.4·f1 + 0.4·f2`. This violates Required result clause 2 (and is precisely the ordering hazard the spec warns about), so all 48 merged tensors will exceed the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance. Secondarily, the required checks are implemented as bare `assert` statements, which are elided under `python -O`, so the run would not fail loudly in that case.
